items.author: Bertha Ismail
items.excerpt: Arusha. East African Community (EAC) member states are strengthening regional cooperation to increase sugar production, expand trade within the bloc and reduce dependence on imports from outside the region, as the industry grapples with a supply deficit of about 1.2 million tonnes. Data from the International Sugar Organisation (ISO) show that the six EAC member states – Tanzania, Kenya, Uganda, Rwanda, Burundi and South Sudan – produced a combined 1.6 million tonnes of sugar in 2025, against estimated annual demand of 2.8 million tonnes.
